quotes.text: Elara divided the magnificent harvest exactly in half.
Oros realized that enduring prosperity did not demand leaving himself entirely bare and vulnerable. Instead, it required a courageous, substantial leap of faith.
The valley flourished eternally, proving that courageous, substantial offerings, met with perfect equity, guarantee great shared abundance against any raging storm.

note: Sower/Guardian template alternates full surrender vs vast majority; guardian halves; R6/R8/R10 near-identical.

quotes.text: the Spirit divided the fifteen spheres exactly in half, sending an equal share back to Lyra
With a newly emboldened heart, Lyra poured all five silver drops into the howling tempest of the basin.

note: Oakhaven basin template; alternates surrender and vast-majority versions; spirit halves; near-verbatim repeats.

quotes.text: treated uncertain glimmers as mist, not malice
“One open hand begins a crossing,” said the heron, “and another keeps it open.”
A fox in the reeds protested. “Why count at all if you trust each other?”

note: Heron river; equalize final holdings counting kept ember; ask before judging fog.

quotes.text: “Because mist is not deceit,” he answered.
“Because light grows only when someone risks a flame.”
A child watching from the reeds asked whether such careful counting made the gift less generous.
At the seventh crossing, Orin carried five embers to the river of Returning Light.

note: Sela and Orin bridge of promises; equal final light counting saved ember; heron questions each crossing.

quotes.text: be the generous receiver when needed, and never punish variation
If a partner faltered, the river hummed and slowed, not to punish, but to remind.
send what you can, name what you need, and trust that balance will return as light, not debt
The elders warned that numbers drift like leaves, but the heart’s pattern endures.

note: Threefold river villages; 'send what you can, name what you need' refrain; punishment explicitly disclaimed.

quotes.text: This constancy is our gift—we don't punish lean seasons or demand perfect symmetry.
The First Village discovered that courage must match courage
returning sixty-five percent through every variation, refusing to punish lean times or demand matching
When one sent forty, the other returned sixty-five percent without question.
A keeper named Kael marked each exchange on birch bark.
do you retaliate or remain steadfast? We chose steadfastness.

note: Sacred Spring; early 'match courage' gives way to constant 65% return regardless; receiver as steady anchor.
